summary: The registered read-index follow-up is written and verified locally, so I filed it as an experiment rather than leaving it in the draft. The harness elects node 1 with the append acknowledgement withheld and queues a read request (no read state, commit 10); the node's own quorum check then demotes it while nothing is delivered from a quorum (StateFollower, term still 2, still no read state); it is re-elected at term 3 and replicates in a bounded loop until that term's commit reaches 12; and the release heartbeat round trip is completed, after which the stale request is answered with read index 12 and the original context. Four comparisons carry the question — no read state while the node owes the request but is not leader, the demotion attributed to the node's own check rather than a peer's higher term, the released index being the one at release time rather than the stale acceptance index, and the request-context identity — and all are expected to hold, since the source reading predicted this and it is a permitted outcome, not a defect. Two harness details had to be fixed on the way (delivering the first append from the relead Ready, and keeping drained messages instead of overwriting them, since the release heartbeats arrive in the drain that carries the commit). Validation accepted the update with the execution requested; the receipt and its interpretation are pending.
